rejected.stem: What type of bond connects amino acids in a protein?
rejected.sourceDefect: Two defensibly correct options: D) Peptide bond is the intended answer, but E) Covalent bond is also correct because a peptide bond IS a covalent (amide) bond. This overlap makes the item ambiguous with no single unambiguous key.

rejected.stem: Which stage of meiosis reduces the chromosome number by half?
rejected.sourceDefect: Ambiguous "when": two options are both defensible for when the chromosome number is halved. Anaphase I (B) is when homologous chromosomes actually separate to opposite poles — the reductional event — but at that moment the single cell still contains 2n chromosomes. Telophase I (D) is when the two haploid (n) daughter cells are actually formed, i.e. the point at which the per-cell chromosome number is genuinely halved. Meiosis I as a whole is the "reduction division," so both B and D are widely cited as the answer in different textbooks, making the item not have exactly one correct option.

Which organ system includes the skin?

Which of the following best describes a gene?
Which of the following is an abiotic factor?
Chemical formula for calcium nitrate:
rejected.sourceDefect: Option B (CaN₂O₆) is atomically identical to option A Ca(NO₃)₂ (Ca1 N2 O6) — it is the same compound written as a collapsed molecular formula. Both A and B are defensible "chemical formulas for calcium nitrate," so the item does not have a strictly unique correct answer. Standard/intended answer is A because it displays the nitrate polyatomic ion, but the composition-identical distractor makes it ambiguous.

rejected.stem: Which process increases H⁺ concentration in solution?
rejected.sourceDefect: Two correct options: B (HCl, strong acid) is the intended answer, but D (CO2) also increases H+ concentration because CO2 + H2O forms carbonic acid (H2CO3 ⇌ H+ + HCO3-), acidifying the solution (e.g., rainwater pH ~5.6). This is a standard syllabus-level fact, not a mere distractor, so the item lacks a unique answer.

In the reaction CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O, what is CH₄?
What is the oxidation number of Cl in NaClO?
Which pair is a conjugate acid-base pair?
rejected.sourceDefect: Minor: option B is written "HCl / Cl" — the chloride ion should be Cl⁻ (missing charge). This does not affect correctness since B is a wrong distractor either way (HCl/Cl⁻ would actually be a valid conjugate pair, so the intended distractor relies on the neutral-atom "Cl" reading). Not disqualifying but worth cleaning to "Cl⁻" is misleading; safest to leave as neutral Cl to keep it wrong.

rejected.stem: Which of these compounds is most polar?
Which gas law relates volume to temperature at constant pressure?
What is the oxidation number of oxygen in H₂O₂?
Which of the following is not a strong electrolyte?
Which solution is most acidic?
Which hydrocarbon is cyclic?
A solution has [OH⁻] = 1×10⁻³ M. What is pH?
Which of the following has a lone pair of electrons?
rejected.sourceDefect: Ambiguous / multiple correct: the stem asks which molecule/compound "has a lone pair of electrons" without restricting to the central atom. Under the literal reading, CO2 (each O carries 2 lone pairs), H2O (O carries 2 lone pairs), and NaCl (Cl- carries 4 lone pairs) ALL contain lone pairs; only CH4 has none. So three of the four options are correct. The intended answer is C (H2O), which works only if the question is silently interpreted as "central atom bearing a lone pair" (O in water vs C in CO2/CH4). This unstated assumption plus the CO2/NaCl distractors also being correct makes the item defective.

Which element has the largest first ionization energy?
Which species is isoelectronic with Cl⁻?
rejected.sourceDefect: Multiple correct answers: Cl⁻ has 18 electrons and is isoelectronic with Ar (18 e⁻), K⁺ (19−1=18 e⁻), AND S²⁻ (16+2=18 e⁻). Three of the four options (B, C, D) are correct, so there is no single correct answer. Only Na⁺ (10 e⁻) is wrong. The item is unusable unless the distractors are changed so exactly one option has 18 electrons.
